evals.prompt: Here's issue #482 as the parent epic for the billing retry feature — break it into implementation slices.
evals.expected_behavior: Fetches the referenced parent issue's body and comments before proposing slice boundaries, rather than slicing from the issue title or number alone, then presents the breakdown for approval.
assertions: Reads the referenced issue's body and comments before proposing slice boundaries
Does not draft slices from the issue title or number alone
Presents the proposed breakdown for approval before creating any tracker issues

evals.prompt: Break this approved PRD into thin vertical implementation issues with dependencies, and show me the breakdown before publishing.
evals.expected_behavior: Proposes tracer-bullet vertical slices (not horizontal layers), each with title, AFK/HITL type, dependencies, user-story coverage, and acceptance criteria, and waits for approval before publishing.
assertions: Breaks work into thin end-to-end vertical slices rather than layer-based tickets
Includes AFK versus HITL classification or equivalent human-review distinction
Presents the breakdown for approval before creating tracker issues

evals.prompt: Break this small feature — add a 'remember me' checkbox to the login form — into issues.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes the work is small enough to need very few slices and does not manufacture unnecessary layer-based tickets like separate database, API, and UI issues for a single small outcome; still presents the minimal breakdown for approval.
assertions: Does not split a small, single-outcome feature into layer-based tickets such as 'database work' and 'UI work'
Produces the minimal number of vertical slices needed to stay independently demoable
Still presents the breakdown for approval before publishing rather than skipping approval because it is small

evals.prompt: Publish the approved issue slices to GitHub in dependency order with real blocker references.
evals.expected_behavior: Creates issues in dependency order using the issue-template shape so blockers reference real IDs, applies only verified labels, and does not invent tracker conventions.
assertions: Publishes or drafts issues in dependency order
Each issue body follows the issue template's section structure
Avoids inventing unverified labels or project fields
Keeps blocker references concrete rather than circular or vague
deterministic_checks: each issue body includes a 'What to build' section
each issue body includes an 'Acceptance criteria' checklist
each issue body includes a 'Blocked by' section (or explicitly states none - can start immediately)

evals.prompt: Write the PRD for this feature before we decide how to split the work.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes product framing is still missing and writes the PRD first (PRD step) instead of guessing at slice boundaries.
assertions: Does not invent implementation tickets when a PRD is still needed
Routes toward the PRD step or product-requirements work instead

evals.prompt: Produce a reusable markdown handoff artifact for the planning and review phase, not tracker-native issues.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes the deliverable is a reusable markdown handoff artifact rather than issue-tracker tickets and routes to workflow-contracts instead.
assertions: Does not force the output into issue-tracker ticket shape when a generic handoff artifact was requested
Routes toward workflow-contracts instead of producing GitHub issue bodies

evals.prompt: Turn everything we know about the billing retry flow into a PRD using the conversation and repo context; only ask if something is blocking.
evals.expected_behavior: Reads the current conversation and the relevant repository surfaces first, inspects the implementation enough to name the major modules likely to change, and only then drafts the PRD — asking a targeted question only if something materially blocking is missing.
assertions: Reads the current conversation and relevant repository surfaces before drafting
Inspects the codebase enough to name concrete modules or surfaces likely to change before writing Implementation Decisions
Does not open with a broad interview; any question asked is targeted at a materially blocking gap

evals.prompt: We've fully discussed the offline sync feature: problem, target users, constraints, and rollout plan are all above. Write the PRD, but we haven't decided yet whether conflict resolution should be last-write-wins or manual merge, and that changes the user stories.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes that problem, users, constraints, and rollout are already settled and does not re-ask about them; asks only the one targeted question about conflict-resolution strategy because it materially changes the user stories and scope, then proceeds to draft.
assertions: Does not re-ask about problem, target users, constraints, or rollout already given in the prompt
Asks at most one targeted question, about the conflict-resolution strategy, because it materially changes scope
Does not stall the whole PRD waiting on unrelated details that were already provided

evals.prompt: Synthesize this feature discussion into a PRD with extensive user stories, implementation decisions, testing decisions, and out-of-scope items.
evals.expected_behavior: Produces a PRD using the required section order from the PRD template, with a user-facing Problem Statement and Solution, an extensive User Stories list covering edge cases and failure paths, Implementation and Testing Decisions grounded in repo evidence with no file paths or code snippets, and an explicit Out of Scope section.
assertions: Problem Statement and Solution are written from the user's perspective, not implementation detail
User Stories list is extensive and covers edge cases, operator/admin roles, or failure/recovery paths where relevant
Implementation Decisions and Testing Decisions contain no file paths or code snippets
Out of Scope section is explicit and present
deterministic_checks: the PRD's section headings appear in this order: Problem Statement, Solution, User Stories, Implementation Decisions, Testing Decisions, Out of Scope
Implementation Decisions contains no file paths (no '/' path fragments) and no code blocks

evals.prompt: Synthesize this feature discussion into a PRD and publish it to the issue tracker if labels and templates are known.
evals.expected_behavior: Produces a complete PRD markdown artifact and only publishes with verified tracker conventions such as real issue labels or templates; otherwise stops at the markdown artifact and surfaces the publication blocker explicitly rather than inventing labels like needs-triage.
assertions: Produces a complete PRD artifact suitable for issue-tracker handoff
Does not invent issue labels such as needs-triage that are not verified in the project
States a publish-or-blocker decision explicitly rather than silently assuming tracker fields exist

evals.prompt: Break this approved PRD into independently grabbable implementation issues.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes the PRD already exists and goes straight to slicing instead of re-authoring it.
assertions: Does not re-author or re-synthesize a PRD when the task is ticket breakdown
Routes toward slicing instead
